survivingClaim: S-periodised explicit formula (Lemma B): for finite S and smooth w of support length T_w, the Krein zero sum of |zeta_S W|^2 equals the archimedean integral plus residues of zeta'/zeta at 1 + 2 pi i k/log p plus a finite prime sum over N_S m m' n <= e^T_w (empty for T_w < log(2 N_S)); re-derived and verified in 13 lane cases plus 5 referee cases to relative 4e-10. For |S|=1, T_w <= log p it gives R_S > 0 for T >= T_0(p,b) via Vinogradov-Korobov (non-uniform threshold). The identity holds for every control with the functional equation and uses only Re s = 1 data. No one-sided inequality on R_S separating zeta from the controls was found: the lower one is the target (P10); the upper depletion law is a long-average mean-value statement (-2 L1(P)) also satisfied by E_a and backward heat on the measured Gaussian windows with zeta's product as multiplier; its every-window form is unproved, with no measured height trend at equal sample size. Off-line pair weights of E_a are damped in size by a partial Euler product (both zeta's and E_a's own), with indefinite sign for the own product. Nothing about zeros of zeta is established.
obstruction: No one-sided inequality on R_S separates zeta from the controls. The lower inequality R_S >= 0 for all tests is the target itself (P10). The upper depletion inequality is the Landau-Gonek mean value -2 sum_{p<=P} log p/(p-1); its every-window form needs a sup-over-height bound on a prime sum outside S and is unproved. R_S tends to 0 as P grows and a partial Euler product damps off-line pair weights, so the multiplier is not an amplifier. The exact S-periodised explicit formula (Lemma B) holds for every control with the functional equation and samples zeta'/zeta only on Re s = 1.

lesson: Putting the Euler product on the test side gives only a mean-value correlation with Lambda (Landau-Gonek); it hides off-line pairs (left partner damped roughly like exp(-li(P^(2 beta-1)))) and sends R_S to 0 as P grows, so it is not an amplifier.
